findings.element: .b-switch span — the "ONE OF THREE" label in the owner's bar (b.css:643-650), on owner-flight, owner-empty, owner-editing, owner-undone, owner-draft and publish, at every width
findings.problem: The label is drawn with a browser-synthesised bold. .b-switch sets font-weight:600 for the project name; .b-switch span then overrides family, size, leading, tracking, case and colour and NOT weight, so the 11px uppercase mono micro-label inherits 600. fonts.css loads Geist Mono at 400 only (measured: document.fonts holds exactly Geist 400, Geist 600, Geist Mono 400), so Chromium smears the 400 outlines. That is a fourth face on a surface whose lock says "Geist 400 and 600, Geist Mono 400. Three faces, no others, no third weight" — and a synthesised face is the one thing a type system cannot ship. Rendered at 4x, a 400/600/400 probe of the same string inside the live document shows the middle line with visibly thickened, blurred stems; in situ "ONE OF THREE" is plainly heavier than "TODAY IS 16 JULY" and "NOTHING TO PREVIEW YET", which are byte-identical in family, size, tracking, case and ink at a real 400 — on owner-empty two of them sit on the same line, 900px apart. Neither gate can see it: audit.mjs checks weight in {400,600} and family in {Geist, Geist Mono} but never the PAIR, and the advance width is unchanged (100.33px at 400 and at 600, because a smear does not move a monospace advance); interaction-check's uppercase-register test (L2038) keys on fontFamily|fontSize|letterSpacing|color and omits weight, so it counts this string as the same object as the real 400 labels. Round 8's refutation of one-of-three-has-no-noun rested on exactly that claim — that this string sits in "the inert-label register that on the very same bar carries 'NOTHING TO PREVIEW YET'". At the pixel it does not.
findings.fix: Add `font-weight: 400;` to the `.b-switch span` rule in b.css, immediately under `font-family: var(--mono);`. Nothing else moves: the string keeps its 11px, its 0.16em, its uppercase and its fore-62, no ladder changes, and the interaction-check uppercase key is unaffected because it never read weight.

findings.element: .b-title's -webkit-line-clamp:2 (b.css:271-284) against over() and clamp() in render-core.js:191-224, on the owner's plan and on the received phone
findings.problem: over() decides overflow with `el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1`. .b-title is set at --lead-head 1.2, but Geist's own line box measures 1.29-1.30em at every size on this ramp (measured with line-height:normal in the live document: 15px->19, 17px->22, 24px->31, 30px->39, 38px->49). A -webkit-box whose text fits on ONE line therefore still reports a scrollHeight larger than its clientHeight, and popping words can never close a gap that is a property of the line box rather than of the width. clamp()'s `while (words.length > 1 && over(el))` runs to the last word and ships it with an ellipsis. Driven at a root of 24px — Chrome's "Very large" text size, one click in Appearance, and the exact reader the file's own comment says the rem half of the ladder exists for — all seven moment titles on the owner's plan at 1440 render as "Menu…", "Send…", "Final…", "Choose…", "Final…", "Venue…", "Wedding…", and the received phone at 390 renders "Menu tasting at…" and "Choose the…". A threshold sweep proves it is a rounding artefact and not real overflow: it fires at root 23, 24 and 28 and does NOT fire at 17-22, 26 or 32. At the default 16px root the margin is one pixel (24px title: scrollHeight 29, clientHeight 29), so the surface is one rounding pixel away from doing this to itself unprompted. Both gates run at a 16px root and cannot see it; interaction-check L2191 only asserts that GUEST titles are never trimmed, and only on the states where the clamp is switched off. This is the lessons library's "silent content deletion" class back on the screen the whole company is judged by.

Round 6 confirmed display-tracking-not-size-graded and its sharpened fix declared five graded steps. The tokens were declared; three of them were never applied, and --track-display was orphaned with them. Measured across every state and width: .b-num at --size-countWide 148px — the desk count, in six owner states, in the received desk state and on the printed keepsake, the single largest object in the composition — renders at -0.04em, the step declared for 96px, because the min-width:701px rule raises the font-size and leaves the letterfit behind. So 96px and 148px carry the same em fit and the bigger one reads looser, when optical letterfit demands the reverse; the declared -0.05em is used nowhere. .b-emptyTitle at 64px and .b-pressTitle at 48px both render at -0.035em — two title-tier sizes on one letterfit, precisely the condition round 6 confirmed — while the -0.038em and -0.032em declared for them sit unused. Only the mono 64 and 96 steps and --track-dayCount landed. Neither gate can see it: audit.mjs keys tracking on family+size+role so each key has one internally consistent occupant, and its ladder-membership test reads every --track-* off :root, so the four dead tokens widen the ladder they were written to tighten.
findings.fix: Apply them — four edits, every value already declared. b.css:1293: add `letter-spacing: var(--track-display-148);` to `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-num, [data-medium="full"] .b-num` beside the `font-size: var(--size-countWide)`. b.css:1313: change `letter-spacing: var(--track-title)` to `var(--track-title-64)`. b.css:1316: change `letter-spacing: var(--track-title)` to `var(--track-title-48)`. shell.css:61: delete `--track-display`, which nothing uses. Each replacement leaves exactly one occupant on its family+size+role key and every value stays on the declared ladder, so both tracking checks stay green.

findings.element: --lead-head: 1.2 (shell.css:82) as taken by .b-title at 17px, and its `margin: 0 0 3px` (b.css:274-277), on phone, day, print and every owner surface below 701px
findings.problem: Geist's own line box is 1.29-1.30em at every size this step governs, so --lead-head is set minus-solid wherever it is used: 1.6px under the box at 17px, 2.2px under at 24px. It is the same setting that makes the clamp above misfire, and on the phone — the screen the brief says decides — it shows in the type itself. A wedding moment name routinely wraps: "Champagne reception on the terrace" sets two lines 20.4px apart at 17px, and cropped at 4x the descenders of line one run into the ascenders of line two. The mono date then sits 3px below, an inset the space ladder exempts rather than declares, so the person's words and the machine's datum fuse into one block whose internal leading is tighter than the leading inside the words themselves — the reverse of the relationship every other pair on this surface draws. The ladder's own comments bind 1.2 to "24, 30, 38px" and 1.5 to "all prose, 13 to 20px"; the 17px title takes neither, and no gate grades a leading against the face it is set in.
findings.fix: In b.css `.b-title`, change `line-height: var(--lead-head)` to `var(--lead-date)` (1.3, already declared, 22.1px at 17px — the first step that contains Geist's box) and change `margin: 0 0 3px` to `margin: 0 0 var(--gap-hair)`. Then restate the desk value in the existing min-width:701px block beside the raise already there at b.css:1310: `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-title, [data-medium="full"] .b-title { line-height: var(--lead-head); }`. Geist|17|head and Geist|24|head each keep exactly one leading, so audit's lead-role check stays green, and every `height <= lineHeight * 1.4` one-line assertion in interaction-check only gets looser.

findings.problem: The count is drawn at three sizes across the artifact — 64px on the unfurl card, 96px on the phone, 148px at every desk width and on the printed sheet — and the word that gives the figure its meaning has one size, 11px, the micro-label step. The figure-to-unit ratio therefore runs 8.7:1 on the phone and 13.5:1 at desk and in print: the same relationship drawn at two very different proportions, and at 148px "days" hangs off the corner of the object the whole composition is built on as a footnote. Driven with a real four-digit count through the empty state (3 October 2029 -> 1175 days), the figure measures 332px across beside an 11px word. It is also the same 11px step as "Sat 1 Aug" and "Edit", so the unit belonging to the biggest thing on the page is set at the size of the smallest. Round 6 established that this display tier has to be graded by size for letterfit; its own satellite was never graded for size.
findings.fix: Step the unit with the count. In the min-width:701px block at b.css:1293, beside `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-num, [data-medium="full"] .b-num { font-size: var(--size-countWide); }`, add `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-unit, [data-medium="full"] .b-unit { font-size: var(--size-data); line-height: var(--lead-body); }` — 13px is a declared ramp step and already the mono data size, and --lead-body is the leading .b-printLinkUrl already carries at Geist Mono 13, so the mono|13|body key keeps one leading and one letterfit and both ladder checks stay green. Baseline alignment inside .b-count is unaffected, and the count/unit assertions in interaction-check read textContent only.

biggestWin: The ladders are bound to ROLES, not to sizes, and all three axes are bound together — a component picks one word and gets its size, its leading and its letterfit as a set. That is what let the sub-fifteen mono tier split into three real objects at one size: "Behind you" (uppercase, 0.16em, fore-62), "Sat 1 Aug" (sentence, 0.04em, fore-72) and "Not going ahead" (sentence, 0.04em, fore-62) now read as a head, a datum and a state rather than as one undifferentiated label — the round-6 monoculture actually dissolved rather than papered over. The reading half of the size ladder is in rem and the display half in px, with the reason written down. Driven across all fourteen states at 390/768/1152/1279/1280/1440 the result holds: not one off-ramp size in three thousand rendered strings, not one line-height:normal, not one widow, not one measure over 75ch except the URL that is meant to be typed, tabular figures on every figure that stacks, and text-wrap balance and pretty chosen per component with an argument attached to each. That is a type system, not a stylesheet with tokens in it.
